title: Rack and pinion
prompt: a rack-and-pinion rig with a sliding carriage on a table with three buttons: “Turn” converts pinion rotation into straight rack travel; “Reverse” moves the carriage back; “Push rack” drives the pinion in reverse; see-through reveals the meshing teeth and conversion between linear and rotary movement
blurb: A bench teaching adaptation demonstrates how a pinion moves a rack and how pushing the rack turns the pinion.
adaptation: Bench adaptation of the named gear-type diagram, not an exact pictured machine. Carriage and supports constrain linear travel. No powered steering is implied.

identity.note: Gears and Belts / Types of Gears / Rack and Pinion Gears, page 37. The Rack and Pinion subsection and car-steering/corkscrew applications are on page 43 in both editions.
identity.mechanism: The rotating toothed pinion meshes with a straight rack to convert rotary motion into linear motion, and driving the rack rotates the pinion.
identity.classificationNote: Only The Wheel and Axle and Gears and Belts are main principle chapters in this unit. Other entries are named examples, diagrams or subsection headings. Greek Mill has both historical context and a named mechanism diagram.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain with explicit principle/application relations. The general rig teaches reversible linear/rotary conversion. Steering wheel applies it to track rods and wheel pivots. Corkscrew applies it to cork extraction. These share the rack-and-pinion principle intentionally; they are not three unrelated new mechanisms.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Catalog and figure metadata establish intended scope only. No existing figure runtime was certified.

prompt.note: The proposed rig faithfully isolates the supported gear principle. It is a bench adaptation of a gear diagram, not a separately pictured complete machine. Avoid implying powered steering or adding a second steering application under this slug.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Explicit bench adaptation of the named gear-type diagram. A carriage and supports constrain the rack in a straight line. Push rack demonstrates the reverse conversion already stated in the source.
